title: Shelf by Shelf - Part Three
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kzApFdb-KEs

Daniel (@dungeondive) devotes the bulk of Part Three to Michael Cisco, an author he considers criminally underground and hopes will one day be as collectible as Thomas Ligotti. *The Divinity Student* is a personal favourite; he walks through the signed limited editions, the challenging later novels he's ambivalent about (*Animal Money*, *Unlanguage*, *Celebrant*), and reads a luminous passage from *The Great Lover* on love and being "ripped to pieces for the one you love." From there a Ray Bradbury section — *Dandelion Wine*, *The Halloween Tree*, and a reminder of just how dark *The Martian Chronicles* really is. The shelf's other pillar is Theodore Sturgeon, whose complete short stories he treasures; he celebrates Sturgeon's "ask the next question" ethos and fearless, boundary-pushing progressivism, singling out *To Marry Medusa* and *Godbody*. He ends on comics, reserving unqualified praise for Katsuhiro Otomo's *Akira* — the best manga art he knows, revisited every few years. A long, affectionate, wide-ranging haul.

----

Cisco or Sturgeon — which of Daniel's "why isn't this more famous?" authors are you most tempted to try first, and why?
